findings.text: Value returning compare and exchange is offered in three bus locking flavors that differ only by the atomicity prefix used, plus sized wrappers that infer the access width from the pointed-to type. The operation compares memory against an expected value and conditionally stores a replacement, reporting the memory content observed at attempt time.

Boolean try form reports success through the processor zero condition and only writes back the observed memory content into the caller supplied expected holder when the exchange did not happen. It is likewise offered in locked, explicitly locked, and processor-local flavors with type-sized wrappers.
Only one, two, four and eight byte widths are supported by the generic exchange paths. Any other requested width is treated as a build time size violation rather than emitting a memory operation.

Synchronization strength is selected by a prefix parameter: configurable SMP prefix, unconditional bus lock, or empty for processor-local use. The memory operand is treated as volatile and compiler memory ordering is fenced around the atomic update.
An integer add primitive is exposed as a thin binding over a generic exchange operation helper, parameterized by pointer, increment and lock prefix choice.

For 32-bit hosts a 64-bit value can be viewed either as one whole quantity or as an ordered low then high 32-bit pair. Eight-byte atomic compare and try operations are built on that split view with locked and local spellings, plus distinct fallback versus direct availability configurations.

For 64-bit hosts a 128-bit value can be viewed either as one whole quantity or as an ordered low then high 64-bit pair. Sixteen-byte value-returning and boolean-try operations are built on that split view in locked and local spellings, while eight-byte local wrappers statically require an eight-byte pointed-to type.
Availability of wide atomic operations is reported by capability predicates tied to processor feature bits for eight-byte and sixteen-byte compare exchange respectively.

Confidential compute vendor is modeled as a three-way choice among none, AMD and Intel when enabled, and as a constant none choice when disabled. The enabled mask accessor returns a global mask value while the disabled accessor returns zero, and random initialization is a no-operation hook.

Compatibility scalar aliases use sixteen-bit storage for mode, user and group identifiers, device numbers, IPC process identifiers and link counts. The compatibility machine string denotes a 32-bit Intel personality with explicit trailing padding.

Compatibility stat carries identifiers and metadata in a fixed sequence from device and inode through permission and ownership fields, then device and size related quantities, then three timestamp pairs each with seconds plus nanoseconds, ending with two reserved words.

Compatibility statfs carries type, block sizing and block counts, file counts, filesystem identifier, name length, fragment size, flags and four spare slots in that order. The architecture declares a need for a packed 64-bit flock compatibility form.

Whether 64-bit time is used in compatibility mode depends on a 32-bit syscall-number flag bit in the current trap register state. X32 context is detected from that same flag when X32 support is compiled in, 32-bit context is the disjunction of IA32 and X32 contexts, and generic compatibility context is defined as 32-bit context.

IA32 context is either unconditionally true in one build configuration or conditioned on emulation being enabled plus a per-thread compatibility status flag in the other. The 64-bit alignment fixup need is defined to be the same condition as IA32 context.
The trap register block for a task is located by starting from that task stack base page, advancing almost a full thread stack minus a small top padding area, then stepping back one register block.
A 32-bit signal information copy helper name is reserved as a self-named marker so an architecture specific implementation takes precedence over a generic one.

In the shown configuration the physical processor identifier query is defined as the boot processor APIC identifier, split-lock and bus-lock setup and handling hooks are no-operation stubs with negative handling results, and feature-control initialization is empty.

Vendor-family-model packing places model in the lowest eight bits, family in the next eight, vendor in the following eight, and reserves the top eight. Companion masks isolate each octet and helpers extract each field or assemble a packed value from separate vendor, family and model inputs.
Three Centaur family-six model numbers are fixed small hexadecimal values for two C7 steppings and one Nano variant. A device table entry validity marker occupies bit zero.

Processor match entries bundle vendor, family, model, stepping range, feature, type and driver data with the validity marker set. Specialized constructors match by vendor plus family plus feature, vendor plus feature, feature alone, vendor plus family plus model, vendor plus family, packed value, packed value plus stepping interval, packed value plus feature, and packed value plus CPU type.

Exception stacks consist of paired guard and usable regions for debug-fault, nonmaskable, breakpoint, machine-check and two confidential-compute vectors, followed by a top guard. One layout uses zero-size guards and optionally empty confidential vectors, while the entry-area layout uses full-page guards and full-size vectors.

Exception stack order is a fixed six-position enumeration ending with a count marker. Helpers derive per-stack byte size, bottom address, top address, structural offset and total page count for the entry-area stack bundle.

The double-fault stack fills one page together with a trailing hardware task state and is page aligned. The per-processor entry area starts with a global descriptor table page, then entry stack with architecture dependent guards, then task state, then guarded exception stacks on 64-bit, then debug store and debug buffer areas, with its total size exposed as a constant.

Per-processor entry data is addressed as a fixed base plus processor index scaled by entry-area size, with a build assertion that the area size is page granular. Entry stack access indexes through that area, and the processor index mapping is either a per-processor stored offset or the identity mapping depending on build configuration.

Feature words are indexed by an ordered enumeration that begins with legacy EDX leaves and Linux-reserved words and then proceeds through numbered ECX, EBX, EAX and extended leaves, terminated by a total word count marker.

Choosing the empty-prefix local exchange form for memory shared across processors removes bus atomicity. Likewise, binding the 64-bit local path to a narrower object violates the width assertion, and assuming nonzero confidential-compute stack space is unsafe when that size is configured to zero.
